written: 2026-09-05, from the diff and the referenced sources, BEFORE the CLI was run (ADR-001: answer key first)

verdicts.FETCH: the bundle should carry a minimal slice; the diff cannot settle it and the source is the project's
verdicts.FLAG: the bundle should state an unverified premise; no file settles it
verdicts.OMIT: the bundle should carry nothing — the reviewer already has it, or it is a dependency's business

rows.why: upload() mass-assigns six columns through updateOrCreate. Whether key/value/type/group/label_ar/label_en are fillable is a real correctness question the diff cannot answer, and it is exactly Experiment 1's model-surface move.
rows.why_not_more: The model is ~25 lines. Nothing above it — the Eloquent base, the builder — adds anything a reviewer of THIS change needs.

rows.why: The lookup filters on page/section/key and then reads $logo->path. Whether those columns exist is off-diff and only the model settles it.
rows.why_not_more: The migration would settle the columns more definitively, but X3 defers a schema resolver; the model surface is the earned move.

rows.why: upload() deletes a file, writes a new file, then writes the database — with no transaction and no cleanup if the write fails. This is a REAL defect: commit 04328a5 later fixed exactly this class of bug across the codebase. A flag naming the unverified premise is the right output.
rows.why_not_more: Resolving it needs the caller and the runtime failure path; fetch-vs-flag.md names this the canonical flag case.

rows.why: The controller's whole return contract is $this->success()/$this->deleted(), inherited through the abstract Controller from the ApiResponse trait. A reviewer cannot judge the response shape without it, and it is project code.
rows.why_not_more: One or two method bodies; the trait's other members are not called here.
rows.known_gap: ADR-A010 forbids the traversal that would reach it (changed file -> Controller -> ApiResponse). Expected to be a FALSE NEGATIVE.

rows.why: Framework-known. Experiment 2: a naked-diff review that knows Laravel catches these unaided. ADR-A011/A013 settle it with a diagnostic and no item.
rows.why_not_more: Fetching the facade or its container binding is the precision failure M1 measured.

rows.why: Eloquent's dynamic static dispatch. The member is the framework's, on the project's class. A Laravel reviewer needs nothing; the model's own surface (E5.1) carries what matters.
rows.known_gap: ADR-A010 blocks Model -> Builder, so these are expected to FLAG. Predicted FALSE POSITIVE.
